properties.doc: A clarification: the truth already existed; the Question dissolves rather than being legislated (contrast Decision, which settles something genuinely open).
An editorial ruling at the parity gates: this claim of a source is deliberately absent from its regeneration and passes forever after. The claim-diff judge consults these rows.

The graph holds the procedure's surface: an asserted signature (inputs, possible outcomes, reads/consults/mutates with per-section open/closed markers) vouched against a prose body via the approved_hash tripwire — validation warns when the approved source drifts. The signature is asserted, so it can lie; the hash catches staleness, not wrongness.

Who should weigh a thing when its moment arrives — a role or group a judgment is routed to, not a named person. The kernel declares only the class: every project's audiences are its own, disclosed by the team or discerned as the ontology evolves. Judgment rows point at theirs via HAS_AUDIENCE.

The graph holds that the procedure exists: a name, a link to where it lives (SPECIFIED_IN), a description. Every signature section is open — a missing edge means unknown, not known-absent. The right level for procedures we neither own nor need the innards of (a DCC tool's million operations).

How much of a procedure the graph holds — coverage, not accuracy (accuracy is guarded by the approved_hash tripwire and derivation answer-keys) and not trust. Procedures point at their level via KNOWN_AT; the per-section *_closed markers are the same dimension at section granularity. The two-axis test decides the level: does an agent need the inner workings, and do we own the source?
User-level subject matter: what the project's things are about (game, story, character, ...). Everything under Concept is domain vocabulary a designer or player would recognize.
A ruling that WAS made: by whom, when. Supersession is EXPECTED — decisions flip as evidence arrives, mechanized via SUPERSEDES.

A kind of concern — the axis a team splits its thinking along. The kernel declares only the class: every project's disciplines are its own (a film crew's are not a game studio's), disclosed by the team or discerned from the corpus as the ontology evolves. Judgment rows point at theirs via HAS_DISCIPLINE, so a parked question can be routed to the kind of thinking it needs.

A holder has one-and-only-one value at a time (a traffic light shows exactly one of red, amber, green). Value-spaces whose members stack are deliberately NOT Exclusive. Declared semantics today; enforcement machinery may arrive with live-state work.
Structural vocabulary: how a concept's value-space behaves. Machinery, deliberately kept out of domain queries.

Subjective, adjudicated knowledge: Questions awaiting decisions, Decisions (with who/when), candidate Inconsistencies and Contradictions awaiting rulings. Supersession expected — judgments flip as evidence arrives.
The metaontology this graph was built with — version and content fingerprint.
The ontology this graph was built with — version and content fingerprint.

A stance held with stated confidence, not yet ruled. Agents mint Opinions during runs (mapping choices, judgment calls, classifications); people hold them too. An Opinion carries its holder and its confidence, is preserved rather than averaged, and binds nothing until ratified — ratification promotes its content into a Decision carrying the ratifier's authority.
Values form a ladder: rank property + bidirectional PRECEDES/FOLLOWS edges. Applied automatically by `ordered: true` on a label.
The concept's value-space contains templates with variables ("Noun of Verbing"-style entries); concrete instances bind each variable via FULFILLS {variable, value} edges, one per variable.

A rule-governed happening: preconditions, inputs and outputs, evaluations, dice, branches, and effects. Exists for comprehension (agents reason about it; code and prose can be generated from it), not direct execution. Every Procedure is KNOWN_AT one of the Completeness levels (see that facet); its possible Outcomes carry plain-English guarantees: read-only, cannot-fail, fails-clean, fails-with-side-effects. Only what cannot be derived is authored: inputs (required/optional), outcome names and guarantees, completeness. Reads, consults, mutates, calls, and outcome effects are derived for transcribed procedures.
Objective knowledge-carriers: artifacts, sources, doc sections — where assertions about the domain come from.
Something genuinely open, awaiting a ruling. Openness is DERIVED — no incoming RESOLVES edge — never flagged. Rows accumulate; nothing is deleted: the tables are the rationale record.

A binding constraint the work must satisfy, held by someone — an individual or a group/org — and checkable where its wording allows. Requirements outrank preference: a dispute between taste and a Requirement resolves for the Requirement, and a dispute about whether work satisfies one resolves at a gate. Supersession is expected, as with any ruling.
Rule-governed transitions exist between values, carried as TRANSITIONS_TO {trigger} edges from an approved transition table.
Known work pending. A Question resolves via a Decision; a TODO resolves via work.

A design message the project weaves through everything it does. Themes are not rules and not flavor: they are intent, stated in the owner's words, and every generated artifact is expected to honor them. The kernel declares only the class: each project's themes are its own ("orthogonality above all" is one corpus's; a storybook's moral is another's).

The graph holds the whole procedure: the approved program is lifted to Step chains and the signature (READS, MUTATES, CALLS, outcomes via HAS_POSSIBLE_OUTCOME) is DERIVED from the body — closed by construction, unable to drift. Derived signature edges land on value citizens; concept-level observations (a branch's subject, a computation's sources) land on the concept's Archetype. Reference resolution goes through the term index — canonical names, aliases, surface forms, and plural variants all resolve; unresolved terms are worklist findings, never silent. Where an approved fact table overlaps the program, a derivation test keeps them in agreement. CAVEAT: derived closure is relative to the graph's VOCABULARY — complete over what the graph can name, silent about what it cannot. The unresolved-term report lists what the source names that the graph does not; each entry is an asterisk on the closure claim.

A named set of graph elements that visibility verdicts speak about — the only permission-bearing unit. kind is knowledge (assume-deny: hidden unless a folded group holds an allow) or masking (assume-allow: removed only when a mask names it); postures are fixed per kind, never switchable. Elements join by IN_CLASS edges or by declared label/type selectors. INCLUDES carries knowledge grant-inheritance (holding the child includes the parent); hierarchical resource trees model as OVERLAPPING MEMBERSHIPS, never as INCLUDES (owner-ruled at the ceremony).

A subject of visibility: who can be granted sight. Individuals are size-1 groups; groups nest via MEMBER_OF, and the transitive fold of a subject's groups is what a visibility lens compiles from. Wearing a subset of one's groups (session activation) and subtracting a group are lens operations, never membership edits.
A normative rule of the two-layer boundary doctrine — one numbered claim, held verbatim.
A run of a conduct record's text — the verbatim body at one heading, ordered within the Procedure it specifies.
An engine design record — a doctrine or design document that is itself canon; the ordered container of its Sections.

A stratum of this graph's own schema. Every graph carries at least two — the Metaontology (the engine's kernel, rank 0, loaded beneath) and the Ontology (this graph's domain vocabulary, rank 1, layered on top) — and every schema citizen DECLARED_IN exactly one. The interrogation path for a fresh connection: ask the Metaontology (what engine family), then the Ontology (what domain), then dig. Future strata (cross-graph stacks, overlays) arrive as instances — the concept is engine-owned; customers interrogate, never edit.
A run of a record's text — the verbatim body at one heading, ordered within its record.

A corpus's structure vocabulary ("Story Units", in the roadmap's language): an ordered ladder of segment types (coarse to fine) whose instances nest via PART_OF chains. Membership test — a segment type subdivides an EXTENDED MEDIUM (text, time, space, film, an execution) into ADDRESSABLE PARTS, readable both as containers ("Round 3", "frame 1042") and as counts ("lasts 3 rounds", "takes 4 T-cycles"). NOT admitted: units of measure as denominations — ruler refinement (1000 g = 1 kg) and scalar quantities (weight, encumbrance) have no addressable instances and stay plain property values. Schemes are DEDUCED from a corpus's artifacts by recon and ratified at a plan gate — never engine-hardcoded — and a corpus may carry several parallel schemes (organizational, temporal, narrative). A project declares a scheme as a facet instance of Segment Scheme with an ordered values: ladder naming its segment types (declared as sibling facet entries); segment types with existing citizen populations bind to their label via that label's concept: list. A segment type declared `recursive: true` may contain any number of children of its own type (a Section holds sub-Sections). A scheme declared `temporal: true` is a time axis: its units are when-vocabulary, and claims may later be scoped to them ("true during this Round") — the scoping machinery arrives with the contradiction work; the declaration is honest now.
A front-door conduct tenet — one numbered claim of how the door speaks, holds trust, and conducts itself; held verbatim.

name: agentic-intake
description: Drive a full graph-native intake end to end — recon, plan gate, scratch authoring via MCP, delta review, canonize, drain to zero. Use when the submitter hands over a source (doc, table, notes) and says "intake this" / "let's ingest X", for any data-plane intake. For classification interviews alone use ontology-intake; for procedure-shaped sources use procedure-intake inside this flow.
---

# Agentic intake

The end-to-end workflow over the intake pipeline (design:
the engine's agentic-etl design record (design/ in the engine repo; graph/engine_docs/design/ inside an installed engine package)). The human appears exactly
twice — the **plan gate** and the **diff gate** — and everything between
is agent + machine loops. Boundary doctrine applies throughout:
`python -m graph docs ontology-doctrine`.

**The invariant:** you author artifacts; only approved artifacts touch
canon; derived layers are never authored by anyone. Your write access is
the `neo4j-scratch` MCP connection ONLY — live is query-only, always.

**The source artifact is inviolable.** The engine never edits the
submitter's material — not a typo, not a heading, and never an *offer*
to edit it. Findings about the source (spelling, ambiguity,
contradiction) surface as suggestions or Question rows for the author
to rule; a ruled correction rides the ingestion with its own Decision
row while the file stays untouched — a source's variant spelling of a
canonical term is absorbed as an alias, never edited in place. Only
the author touches the artifact.

**Tables sit one notch looser, by written rule (owner-ruled): the
engine PROPOSES table changes and edits a data file only under
explicit owner dictation, recorded verbatim in a Decision row.**
Everything else lands graph-side and the file simply lags canon —
lagging sources are legitimate, silent table edits are not. The
destination is full table inviolability once every instrument reads
canon instead of sources; until then, dictation-with-receipt is the
only door. **File deletions are the strictest dictation class**: a
deletion lands only on an own-words imperative from the owner
("delete it"), never on agreement-by-number to a recommendation —
agreement is a sufficient receipt for edits, one grade too weak for
destroying a file. **Dictated table edits are CSV-aware**: a phrase
replacement that introduces a comma into an unquoted cell corrupts
the row silently. After every table edit, verify every row's column
count and run the corpus build — post-flip, the graph suite does not
read the tables; only the corpus build does, and a green suite proves
nothing about them.

label: [Conduct Section]
name: Attribution: every claim seeks its graph home

properties.body:
## Attribution: every claim seeks its graph home

After parity, the census (the engine's attribution module, wired into the
roundtrip scorecard): every draft claim is attributed against canon on
the graded source ladder — a citizen's structured properties, its
carried receipts, or a long-prose home (the soup rung: attributed AND
a named intake debt). The matcher reads STRUCTURE, not just prose: a
claim that names both endpoints of a ground edge and speaks the edge
type's words homes first-class on both citizens, and a claim found in a
procedure's lifted step text homes at receipt grade citing the
procedure — both mechanical, no synonyms (that stays the ruled-mappings
tier). A homeless claim splits on parity's verdict: if
the original says it, it is a CANON GAP — surfaced with an auto-filed
debt, shipping never stops, at any density; if parity called it
invented, it is an UNATTRIBUTED INVENTION — a red presented WITH the
artifact, named in the margin, never a hidden parked run. The whole
submitted artifact is the judging unit (`python -m graph roundtrip
--book`); sections are internal drill-down. The original remains the
parity reference until the owner explicitly declares succession — no
milestone implies it.

label: [Conduct Section]
name: Canon changes (full flow: the agentic-intake skill)

properties.body:
## Canon changes (full flow: the agentic-intake skill)

Canon changes never happen here. Scratch authoring, `python -m graph
delta`, approval, and `python -m graph canonize --apply` (graph-native:
verify-all-before-apply-any, re-derivation, backup re-export, chained
event log) are the agentic-intake skill's territory — this skill only
keeps the databases healthy around that flow. After an apply, the
ritual: pytest → commit the export + round archive + event-log line in
one change set → next round cuts scratch fresh.

## Cautions

- **Two gates, always.** No matter how mechanical the intake looks, the
  plan gate and diff gate are never skipped or merged.
- Branch from `origin/main` explicitly; issue-first; no commits without
  explicit per-ship authorization in the current conversation.
- Reports are the user interface: anything you surface to a human
  follows the error doctrine (Attempted X / context Y / failed due to Z,
  collated, with remedies).
- **Gate presentations are human prose, not pipeline prose**: lead
  with what changes in the CORPUS's terms — "each rank in the ladder
  gets its behavior sentence attached" — one plain sentence per fact.
  Delta/canonize/node/edge vocabulary stays in the linked reports;
  the approver should never need the machinery glossary to approve their
  own content.
- Draft-then-verify discipline: claims about what the machinery will
  derive are tested against the machinery (run the tools), not asserted.
  **A dry run proves only the stages it actually executes** — a
  verification that lives in the apply alone (re-derivation, a
  completeness census) can refuse a round the dry run waved through.
  Never present a dry run as evidence that findings "don't block";
  either run the blocking stage or state aloud which stages the dry
  run skipped.
- If the source is quirky-formatted, write the normalized canonical
  intermediate (approver-approved, hash-pinned) rather than proposing
  engine parsers — the kernel does not grow per artifact.
- **Engine asks are parser-era scaffolding.** The named one-line
  machinery ask (`skip_values` set the model: shape + blast radius,
  its own test, lands only on an explicit yes) is the CURRENT
  correct form when an artifact wants a primitive the engine lacks.
  It sunsets with the fixed parsers: once agents read artifacts
  natively, a novel table shape is a comprehension problem, and the
  destination CX never surfaces engine internals to a submitter at
  all. Prefer shapes that need no engine change; never work around a
  missing primitive with a lesser default.
- **Engine additions speak no project vocabulary.** Docstrings,
  comments, and test names inside engine code draw their examples from
  an imaginary domain, never from the host project's — the
  vocabulary-leak test enforces it, and a leak found at review is a
  rewrite, not an exemption.

## Cautions

- **Missing engine primitive = Tier 3 when a second consumer exists.** A gap
  in the engine (no `bool` type, no inverse for an existing edge
  shape, ...) is a Tier 2
  observation *only* if you would genuinely live with the workaround forever.
  The moment a second consumer is visible — another CSV, a TODO-block line —
  it becomes an owner decision: surface the primitive, do not bury a
  text/string workaround in the plan as the default. A column of yes/no
  markers (`Y`/`N`, `✓`, blank-for-false, ...) is a boolean — propose the
  `bool` type, never a `text` flag storing the raw marker. Check what the
  column's truthy/falsy vocabulary actually is; the marker varies by table.
  (Landing the engine change is still gated by the `graph/*.py` bright-line;
  surfacing it in the plan is not.)
- Genuine taxonomy (a citizen is a KIND of a concept, not an instance of
  it) is declared on the concept entry (`subtypes:`) and derived by the
  engine at every rebuild — never authored as ground edges. Activating
  it for a project's first case is a kernel ceremony: explicit owner
  dialogue, recorded as a Decision.
- Placeholder pollution: prose fragments make bad placeholder nodes — use
  `on_missing: report` for mixed-content columns.
- Comma-splitting fragments clauses that contain commas; the report catches
  them — read it.
- The owner rules all naming. Full-text names over abbreviations
  (aliases map the CSV codes). Check docs for canonical terminology before
  proposing names — the docs outrank the README, which outranks the CSVs.
- **Edge naming is STRATIFIED** (owner ruling): (1) kernel/facet
  mechanics (INSTANCE_OF, PRECEDES/FOLLOWS, TRANSITIONS_TO, FULFILLS) stay
  generic — they belong to the facet, not a domain; (2) parallel domain
  systems are domain-explicit, always — two systems with same-shaped
  tiers get HAS_<SYSTEM-A>_TIER and HAS_<SYSTEM-B>_TIER, never one
  shared edge; (3) one system with many participants shares a name
  and splits only if the system splits; (4) with no parallel yet but a
  foreseeable collision, name preemptively-explicit
  (CONSUMES_<RESOURCE> when other consumables are foreseeable). Do
  not propose polymorphic reuse across parallel systems.
- No commits, ever, without explicit authorization in the current
  conversation.

## Cautions

- An example in the source gets the standing disambiguation question
  (preserve verbatim vs. regenerate as illustration) — never a silent
  default. Forward references get the ordering-intentional question.
- A sentence the machine cannot parse is flagged as a QUESTION — "I
  didn't understand this; is it garbled?" — never asserted as a source
  defect ("garbled", "malformed"), and it never blocks work (owner
  ruling: a hard-to-parse sentence may be exactly as intended). The
  incomprehension rides the margin as a low-confidence Opinion; the
  owner's reply threads to it as the Answer.
- Carried-verbatim storage keeps original bytes; normalized forms are
  matching keys only.
- Park, never die: a blocked or disconnected run keeps its state and
  resumes; the owner should never need to say "try again."

## Cautions

- Do not invent cases the prose does not define — when a corner has no
  case, model the absence and mark it with a comment.
- Guarantees and outcome names are DESIGNER decisions; a plausible draft
  is a proposal, marked REQUIRES DESIGNER REVIEW.
- Before promising any derived edge, name the projection arm that emits
  it — the scanner contract lives in the Transcribed doc string (on the
  graph) and data/procedures/README.md; expectations about projections
  are claims to dry-run, not hopes.
- No probabilities, ever (owner ruling). Uncertainty is open/closed
  closure + Judgment adjudication.
- Two-stage approval protects determinism: extract now, the approver
  approves, the ETL consumes only the approved artifact.
- No commits without explicit authorization in the current conversation.

name: Dispatch — which job serves the input

properties.body:
## Dispatch — which job serves the input

The designer's input arrives as conversation. Classify it and invoke
the job; never make the designer name a job.

| The designer... | Invoke | Door renders |
|---|---|---|
| hands over an artifact (text, image, model, audio, link) | the intake flow (agentic-intake) | progress silently; the gate at the end |
| asks what/why/how about their world | the query flow (graph-query) | the cited answer (T11) |
| asks for a draft or deliverable | the generation flow | the deliverable, plus what needed judgment |
| annotates, rules, or debates | this skill directly | the thread (below) |
| asks "show me the machinery" or names a reference number | forensics | the raw record or technical report, verbatim |

The jobs' own output (reports, verdicts, progress) is never shown
directly — the door re-renders it. The one exception is forensics: on
request, raw records are handed over untranslated.

# Dynamic-ontology intake

Scope note: this skill is the CLASSIFICATION AND INTERVIEW discipline —
it powers the plan gate. For a full end-to-end intake (scratch authoring
via MCP, delta review, canonize, drain to zero) use the **agentic-intake**
skill, which invokes this one at its step 2.

Boundary context: `python -m graph docs ontology-doctrine` — **intake grows the
PROJECT layer only.** If the artifact demands something kernel-shaped (a new
root, a new common facet), that is a Judgment moment: raise it as a Question
for design dialogue; never resolve it inline.

The hypothesis this procedure serves (validated on early table
mappings, ~80/20): most of a mapping falls out mechanically; the remainder isn't noise —
it's the artifact's most interesting design questions. Surface them; the
owner answers them; many become Judgment-root material.

## Failure triage

- `Connection refused` → Desktop DBMS not running.
- `Unauthorized` → `.env` doesn't match the DBMS credentials (MCP reads
  the same `.env` via its launcher; it needs a reconnect after
  credential fixes). The live connection's user is read-only by design —
  a write refusal on live is the boundary working, not a bug.
- Validation errors naming the ontology → fix `graph/ontology.yaml` (or
  stop and talk to the owner if the fix is semantic).
- Apply refuses because the live database drifted from the backup →
  `python -m graph restore`, then retry.
- New warnings after a data edit → often the point: read them as
  findings, file issues for genuine data problems (issue-first
  convention).

## Gate conduct

- **Lead with an example** at every built-work gate: the command, the
  expected output, one thing to break. Explanation after, never instead.
- **Rulings ride chat, not review-panel comments.** Inline plan-panel
  comments have been lost in transit — anything not in the chat or a
  file does not exist. Number every question on the collated sheet so
  the owner can rule tersely by number; if panel comments arrive
  anyway, echo them back in chat before acting on them.
- **State the database picture** at every gate and demo: which database
  currently shows what (live = branch state during a round; merged main
  returns on reconcile).
- **End every gate with the Question harvest line**: "N new Questions
  filed this round — rule any now, or all park."
- **Churn is healthy** — mid-gate rulings are adversarial review
  working. At a THIRD substantive ruling in one gate, OFFER a follow-on
  round split; the approver decides. Never engineer the churn away.

## Gate voice

- **Shape: asks first, decisions second, elucidation last.** Every gate
  opens with **"here are the asks"** — a numbered list of exactly what
  the approver must do or rule on — then **"here are the decisions I
  made"** — judgment calls already taken — then the context and
  reasoning for whoever wants them. Never a storytelling lead-in: the
  reader must tell at a glance what needs them versus what is handled.
- **The narratives' five voice rules govern gate presentations BY
  DEFAULT, for every submitter — including the owner.** Machinery
  vocabulary (proposal ids, version numbers, command names, Cypher)
  appears only below a marked "the machinery, for the record" fold, or
  when the submitter asks in kind. The owner's stated preference
  (plain gates, machinery on request) is recorded by identity against
  the empathic-presentation Question.
- **Self-check BEFORE SENDING any gate — run the list per gate, every
  gate; the same-message rule has now failed two independent sessions
  when left to memory:**
  1. Asks → decisions → elucidation, in that order?
  2. Does every question grid carry its FULL context **in this same
     message** — the decision, the evidence, each option's
     consequences, a recommendation? The approver must be able to rule
     from this message alone; context living two messages back is a
     defect.
  2b. Is the context CITED, not paraphrased? Quote the actual sources
     verbatim — the artifact's sentences, the graph record's own text,
     the tracker item's words — each labeled with where it lives, then
     name the tension between them explicitly, then pros/cons per
     option in prose. Narrative ABOUT the sources is not context; an
     approver who cannot see the raw material cannot rule. And if the
     approver rejects a grid or asks for context, the next message is
     evidence and prose only — re-offering a grid immediately, however
     enriched, reads as hammering; let them rule in their own words.
  3. One re-read in the submitter's domain terms only — any sentence
     needing the machinery glossary gets rewritten or moved below the
     fold.
  4. Are answers to the submitter's direct questions in the turn's
     FINAL message — never only in between-tool status text, which the
     submitter may never see?

Canon is the only source of facts; steering shapes presentation. Use whenever the owner asks to generate something from canon.

# Generation

Every generated artifact is a projection of the graph into a medium.
The graph supplies the facts; the owner may supply steering; the medium
supplies the form. The full design this skill implements is
the engine's agentic-approach design record (design/ in the engine repo; graph/engine_docs/design/ inside an installed engine package) (v3: Virtues, Tenets, Method); this file is the
working procedure.

## Holding a thread

When the designer pushes back on an item instead of answering it:

- Marshal canon's evidence **both ways** — counts, citations,
  precedents, and what canon lacks — and hand the ruling back (T9).
  Never a side, never a taste.
- "What breaks if I say yes?" is answered with the referencing
  facts, counted and cited, pulled live from canon.
- Absence is stated plainly and paired with the offer to record an
  open question (T14).
- The thread ends in a record (T15): the ruling with the designer's
  words, or an open question. Before answering a resurfaced
  question, query the Judgment records for prior rulings on the same
  subject — a returning question is presented *with its prior thread*,
  never cold.

properties.body:
## Idioms that matter (each learned the hard way)

- **Ordered collect**: `collect(x ORDER BY ...)` is invalid; sort before
  aggregating: `WITH c ORDER BY c.rank RETURN collect(c.name)`.
- **Post-aggregation ORDER BY** can't see pre-aggregation variables; project
  them into the `WITH` first.
- **Placeholders skew counts.** Real entities: `WHERE n.placeholder IS NULL`.
  Placeholder nodes are queryable dangling references — often the answer IS
  the placeholder (that's a data finding, cite the issue if one exists).
- **Ladders**: compare with `rank` (`a.rank > b.rank`), traverse with
  `PRECEDES`/`FOLLOWS` (single hop = adjacent tier).
- **"What kind of thing is X"**: full chain via
  `MATCH p=(v {name:$x})-[:INSTANCE_OF*]->(top) WHERE NOT (top)-[:INSTANCE_OF]->() RETURN [n IN nodes(p)|n.name]`.
- **The facet menu is data**: instances of the `Facet` archetype, with `doc`
  properties explaining each.
- **Matrix-edge semantics live in the cookbook**, beside the worked
  query — which party's number a matrix cell holds is a per-edge fact;
  check there before interpreting a modifier.

## Input layers (the evaluator boundary)

The original artifact — and ANY judge finding that quotes it — is
evaluator-internal: it never enters a generator's brief or readable
set. A verdict that quotes the missing content is the answer written
in the margin; feeding it back launders the original into the draft
through the evaluator. Feedback crossing down to a generator is
REDACTED to defect class plus citizen pointers ("a claim carried by
(Beast) the Cinder Fox is missing — consult that citizen"), which forces
the fix through the graph. Generators read canon, the brief, and the
owner's steering — nothing else. Drafters RECORD the citizens they
consult as rows on the run trace: that consulted set is what makes a
citation earned (the engine attribution module's strong form); an unearned-but-
correct claim is re-derived with the citizen provisioned, invisibly —
the trace records both passes.

## Mapping and drafting lessons

- **Design-intent prose sorts five ways at intake — never into one
  "philosophy" bucket.** Premise (the world's terms), authorial intent
  (what the work is for), REQUIREMENTS (binding directives, checkable
  where worded so — kernel Judgment citizens), theses (claims about how
  the system behaves — several verifiable), and rationales (why a
  mechanic is shaped so — these attach to their mechanic as doc-notes,
  never stand alone). Premise/intent/theses home under the kernel Theme
  concept; requirements become Requirement rows; the sort question is a
  standing intake habit beside Units and ladder-direction.
- **A worked example gets a disambiguation question at intake, never a
  silent default: "preserve this exact example word-for-word, or treat
  it as one illustration the system may regenerate from the mechanic?"**
  The two fates have different homes (a carry-verbatim row vs. a
  regenerable render), and only the owner knows whether the example's
  particular wording is the point.
- **A forward reference in source prose ("described later", "see the
  end of this chapter") gets a disambiguation question at intake: is the
  ordering intentional?** If yes, the ordering is a claim to carry; if
  no, the reference is glue a regeneration may replace with a better
  cross-reference. Never decide silently in either direction.
- **Normalizing stored text must never lose information.** If a
  registry keys by a normalized form (case-folded, whitespace-collapsed),
  the original bytes are stored beside the key — normalization is for
  matching only. A store that cannot reproduce its input verbatim is
  distorting it.
- **A carried-verbatim row's name key is the whitespace-collapsed,
  lowercased passage** (`" ".join(text.split()).lower()` — trailing
  punctuation KEPT), with the original bytes in its text property. This
  is NOT the judge's sentence normalization (which strips trailing
  punctuation); confusing the two produces rows the matcher silently
  never finds. Read an existing row and mirror it exactly.
- **Scope notes are predictions, not boundaries.** When a source
  changes, recon verifies the FULL citation set — every program and
  citizen citing that source — never just the subset the plan
  predicted. A citation the plan missed, found at recon, is a
  footnote; found mid-round, it is an interjection.
- **A relationship the source states in a column may already be canon —
  check under its DECLARED edge-type name before authoring it.** When the
  schema maps a source column to an edge type, a bootstrap load may have
  already materialized those edges; re-authoring them duplicates or trips
  a uniqueness constraint. Read the edge type's exact name from the schema
  and query for it — never probe with a guessed name and conclude "absent"
  from a miss (a guessed name returns zero while the real edges sit under
  the declared one). The same holds for template-instance bindings and
  per-member value tags: verify what the load already carried before
  proposing to add it, so the round authors only the genuinely-new.
- **Give every new label its `doc:` string AT MAPPING TIME, drawn
  verbatim from the chapter.** Chapter prose without a canon home keeps
  regenerations red and forces a second schema round. The label `doc:`
  is the canon home for section-level prose; Theme citizens home thesis
  sentences; Quote citizens home quoted material with attribution.
- **Procedure nodes are ground facts**: they enter canon through
  scratch + delta carrying body (the full approved YAML text),
  completeness, closures, inputs/outputs, source, source_path (mirror
  an existing transcribed Procedure node). `rederive` alone never adds
  them — it lifts Steps/Outcomes FROM the ground body at derivation.
- **A program file approved in a prior round does not prove its citizen
  landed.** A round has shipped approved program files while forgetting
  their ground nodes, and the gap surfaced only when a later round went
  looking. During recon (and again at delta self-review), diff the
  schema's approved-program file list against the working graph's
  procedure citizens; any file without a citizen is prior-round debt —
  land it with the opening move, and file the finding as its own issue.
- **Chapter drafts of procedure-cited sections must embed the rendered
  program** (`python -m graph generate "<name>"`) — the roundtrip's
  procedure tier judges the rendering's claims, not just the prose.
- **Cold-draft formatting**: the claim splitter treats `*` bullets as
  paragraph continuations (only `-`/`+`/`1.` start units) — separate a
  lead-in line from a `*` bullet block with a blank line or their
  claims merge and the lead-in reads as omitted.
- **Quote program text that carries YAML-active characters.** An
  unquoted scalar silently truncates at ` #` (an inline citation eats
  the rest of its sentence) and breaks the parse at `: ` (a colon-space
  mid-sentence reads as a nested mapping). Provenance lives on Judgment
  rows, not in body text; quote any step that needs punctuation.
  Validation carries a tripwire for the silent case (a ` #` tail that
  vanished in parsing is flagged with its line number), and `generate`
  remains the eyes-on check.
- **Program bodies sync from their approved files — never by hand.**
  After editing a program file, `python -m graph delta --sync-bodies`
  rewrites the working graph's copy from the file; every delta run
  verifies the sync across the whole working graph and refuses by name
  when a body drifted. The paste-and-hash ritual is retired. A
  chapter-spanning program lists every section it draws from
  (`specified_in.section` takes a list); receipts check against all of
  them.
- **A concept rename re-points its ground anchors in the same
  changeset.** Ground edges anchored to a machine node survive
  re-derivation only while the concept stays declared — a rename
  orphans them silently. Query the machine node's incoming ground
  edges before renaming; re-point them to citizens that survive (the
  machine layer is never authored by hand, so a vanished endpoint
  cannot be recreated from scratch).
- **Answer keys**: cells meaning "no value exists here" beyond the
  global empty markers (a project's special glyphs) are declared per
  key with `skip_values:` — never patched into the engine's
  EMPTY_MARKERS.

## Posture

- **Graph first, files second.** The graph is canon
  (the flip): it holds the normalized names, values, and the metamodel —
  one query beats a grep across dozens of source files, and the source
  files may legitimately lag canon. Fall back to docs only for prose
  the graph doesn't hold yet, or when the graph is unavailable.
- **Read-only, always.** Use `mcp__neo4j__read_neo4j_cypher`. The live
  connection rides a read-only database user (writing is physically
  impossible) and the write tool is denied by settings; canon changes
  flow only through the delta path (agentic-intake skill).
- Worked, verified queries live in `graph/cypher/cookbook.md` — start there
  and adapt.

## Presentation is its own check

An evaluator that judges content order-free is blind to placeholder
headers, misordered ladders, misaligned cells, and collapsed table
structure. Rosters with a declared order render in that order; cells
hold their positions under named headers; structure-reflecting
sections (a table of contents) generate LAST. Verify presentation
separately from content parity — human or scripted.

## Procedure

1. **Read the artifact cold**, plus any docs that embed or describe it.
2. **Classify against the existing ontology, in three confidence tiers** —
   report all three explicitly. **Verify candidates against the source
   tables by FULL name, never by name fragments** — a fragment query
   misses template instances and long-form names, and a wrong
   "nothing defines this" claim has minted a redundant stub over an
   existing template. When claiming absence, read the table.
   - **Tier 1, mechanical** (would auto-propose): exact column-header matches
     to existing catalogs; cell values resolving to existing node names
     (through aliases); edge shapes already in the vocabulary.
   - **Tier 2, observations** (flag, don't act): near-matches, sibling
     patterns, sentinel values, terminology drift.
   - **Tier 3, genuine owner questions** (the 20%): concept classification,
     facet membership, naming, modeling choices, and **missing engine
     primitives a second consumer already wants** (see the missing-primitive
     rule in Cautions). Never answer these yourself.
3. **Read the facet checklist from the graph**, not from memory:
   instances of the `Facet` archetype (with `doc` explanations). Ask of the
   new concept: ordered? exclusive? stateful? — one question per facet.
   **For every ordered ladder, establish its DIRECTION** (owner rule):
   ascending, descending, or neither — deduce it from the artifact's own
   mechanics where possible, and where it is not clear to deduce, ask
   the owner. Record the answer where the ladder is declared. Rules
   prose saying "above/higher" over a ladder whose direction was never
   pinned is exactly how opposite readings of the same sentence survive
   into play.
4. **Resolve Tier 3 by scenario interview**: pose concrete situations
   from the corpus's own world, engineered so different answers imply
   different classifications. Expect the owner to redirect to
   prose — read the cited docs and come back with findings. Expect judgments
   to flip; that's the process working.

   **The interview is ONE collated question sheet — never a stream.**
   Serial questioning — one ping at a time, context scattered across
   messages, the owner put on the spot — is not a permitted interview
   shape, however urgent a single question feels. Instead: finish the
   recon, compose EVERY owner question, then present them together as
   one sheet the owner reads at their own pace and answers in any
   order. On the sheet, each question is BUILT with its context, not
   dressed at presentation: the evidence quoted verbatim (the
   artifact's sentences, the graph record's own text — each labeled
   with where it lives), the tension between them named explicitly,
   what each answer would do, and a recommendation. A question the
   owner cannot rule on from its entry alone is not ready for the
   sheet — hold it and gather the missing context first. Follow-ups
   spawned by an answer join the NEXT collated sheet (or the diff
   gate), never an immediate counter-question; after a rejected or
   challenged sheet, the next message is evidence and prose only.
   (This mirrors the convergence loop's one-collated-escalation-gate —
   the shape that has never drawn a complaint. agentic-intake's
   gate-voice self-check enforces the same rules at presentation time;
   the discipline starts here, where the questions are made.)
5. **Prose rule (two-stage, protects ETL determinism)**: never have the build
   interpret prose. Extract a structured proposal (table/YAML) from prose
   NOW, with the owner; the approver approves it; the approved artifact goes
   in git; the deterministic ETL consumes only that. Mark all extracted
   content as REQUIRING DESIGNER REVIEW.
6. **File findings as issues** (issue-first convention): data problems,
   terminology drift, rules gaps — one issue per finding class, presenting
   options without deciding them.
7. **Implement only after the owner rules**: ontology.yaml entry
   (concept list, ordered flag, catalog, properties, relationships — with
   `on_missing: placeholder` for name-like columns, `report` +
   `unmatched_property` for prose-like columns), then the maintenance
   loop (see the rebuild-graph skill): validate → rederive (the backup
   re-export rides it; golden in the same change set) → test → restore
   scratch → MCP verify.
8. **Update the TODO block** in ontology.yaml (remove the mapped file, note
   deferred aspects) and record deferred machinery explicitly (e.g.
   "TRANSITIONS_TO awaits docs spike").
9. **The glossary stage**: run `python -m graph terms` after mapping. New
   citizens often resolve old unresolved terms; whatever remains gets
   classified (surface form/alias | stub concept | pending_instance |
   reject), never silenced. When a mapped label absorbs a stub concept's
   territory, graduate its pending_instances into real rows and delete the
   stub — the worklist (`MATCH (s:Archetype {stub: true})`) should shrink
   with every intake.

## Procedure

1. **Read the source cold** (doc section, catalog entry, external doc).
2. **Author/derive discipline** — propose ONLY what must be authored:
   - `inputs` (required/optional + `when_absent` defaults). Inputs are
     caller-supplied; things the procedure observes are READS — derived,
     never authored for transcribed procedures.
   - **Every non-obvious authored fact carries a `from_text:` receipt** — a
     verbatim quote of the source sentence it was extracted from. The
     extractor verifies the quote appears in the source; review reads claim
     beside evidence. An interpretation without a receipt is an
     unfalsifiable paraphrase — a plausible-reading extraction once
     inverted the source's meaning entirely; the receipt would have
     collapsed it on contact.
   - `possible_outcomes` names + guarantees (`read-only` / `cannot-fail` /
     `fails-clean` / `fails-with-side-effects`). Guarantees are rules facts the
     body cannot reveal — always ask the owner ("does a failed X leave
     the cost paid?").
   - `completeness`, `specified_in` + `approved_hash` (sha256 of the source body,
     computed the way the extractor compares it: DocSection body or the
     node's description property).
   NEVER hand-write reads/consults/mutates/calls for a transcribed
   procedure — the projection derives them, and hand-written copies drift.
3. **Draft-then-plan** — author the candidate YAML in the scratchpad
   DURING planning and run `python -m graph validate` and
   `python -m graph generate` against it (add the draft to a scratch
   ontology copy if needed). The plan quotes ACTUAL tool output — a plan
   containing untested claims about what the machinery will derive is not
   ready to present. (Both cold-test misses were machinery assumptions
   not traced through code.)
4. **Assess by scenario dry-run** — the extraction method IS the interview:
   walk boundary cases with the owner ("the resource exactly equals
   the cost — which branch?"). Adjudications become guards. Expect the prose to blur
   at least one boundary; that blur is the artifact's most valuable find.
5. **The owner names everything — and rules everything, explicitly.**
   Outcome names are the vocabulary in-world agents will enumerate:
   propose candidates
   from stop prose; the owner rules. **Ask outcome name and guarantee
   TOGETHER, as separate answers — a ruling on the name is not a ruling on
   the guarantee, and nothing is ever inferred from silence** (a
   header-flagged proposal relies on the approver rereading the file).
   Same stop text in two branches = same outcome (deliberate); distinct
   prose joining one outcome uses the inline `stop: {outcome:, note:}`
   form. Carry the source's terminal sentence whole into stop prose,
   including onward-flow clauses — a dropped trailing clause has been
   the late-found extraction gap more than once.
6. **Grammar discipline** — match every `when:` condition against the
   approved grammar (see data/procedures/README.md). Anything new is a
   grammar-extension PROPOSAL for the owner, not a free-form condition.
   Prefer two `when`s over inventing an `or`.
7. **Bijection and closure audits** before presenting (largely already
   done if step 3 ran the tools against the draft):
   - every stop claimed by exactly one outcome; every outcome claims ≥1
     stop (`python -m graph validate` enforces this)
   - every declared input used in the body; every non-graph name in the
     body either an input or flagged
   - attested level: every section explicitly `closed: true/false`, with
     "what evidence would close this?" asked per open section
8. **Generation-diff fidelity check** — `python -m graph generate "<name>"`
   and diff against the source prose. The render covers the WHOLE
   signature (inputs, outputs, precondition, steps) — an authored input
   the source never states shows up as an invention. Source facts missing
   from the render are extraction gaps; rendered facts missing from the
   source are inventions. Do not present until inventions are zero.
9. **Answer-key hunting** — does an approved fact table exist that the
   program should reproduce (a transition table, an effects matrix)?
   Wire a walk-derivation test (`walk_transitions` == the relevant rows).
   If no table exists, ask whether the derived facts should become one.
   **Numeric worked examples are recompute candidates**: an example
   that asserts numbers can become a fixture row whose every asserted
   value is recomputed from the approved tables (`derives: recompute`),
   only the random inputs taken on faith — and recomputing examples
   during RECON, before any extraction, has surfaced real
   source-vs-data contradictions; treat it as a recon step, not just a
   test artifact.
10. **The glossary stage** — read the unresolved-term report
   (`unresolved-term` section of graph/reports/validation.md; the sweep
   command is `python -m graph terms`). Every hit gets CLASSIFIED, never
   silenced: a surface form or alias of an existing citizen | a stub
   concept (recognized-but-unmodeled; check the worklist first:
   `MATCH (s:Archetype {stub: true})`) | a pending_instance of a stub or
   label | a program `locals:` entry. The glossary IS the graph — terms
   resolve to citizens, and an unmapped system a program consults should
   be a stub concept, not a textual workaround. Read the source anyway.
11. **Unknowns exit as Judgment citizens** — load-bearing open questions
   become data/questions.csv rows (ABOUT the procedure), never resolved
   inline. Model the prose literally; record the gap.

Then landing: the approved YAML enters canon as a ground Procedure node
through the delta path (agentic-intake skill); derivation lifts
Steps/Outcomes from the body. **Before the new file's first delta, diff
its top-level key-set against an approved file of the same completeness
level** — a stray key the reader does not expect is refused at apply,
and the check is free at authoring time where the refusal costs a full
approve-apply cycle. Verify via MCP (HAS_POSSIBLE_OUTCOME
table, CALLS trace, outcome assignment edges, KNOWN_AT levels).

name: procedure-intake
description: Assess a procedure (source prose describing a process, an in-world resolution, an external tool operation) and produce the right approved artifact for its Completeness level — a full program (transcribed), an asserted signature (attested), or a bare reference (cited). Use when the submitter says "let's intake/program/transcribe procedure X" or when a source section describes a process.
---

# Procedure intake

Scope note: when a procedure-shaped source arrives as part of a broader
intake, the **agentic-intake** skill drives the overall flow and this
skill governs the procedure content at its plan gate (step 2).

Boundary context: `python -m graph docs ontology-doctrine` — Procedure, the
Completeness vocabulary, Step, and Outcome are ENGINE machinery
(graph/metaontology.yaml); the procedures themselves are project artifacts
(data/procedures/*.yaml). Program vocabulary grows by owner approval, never by
improvisation.

---
name: graph-query
description: Answer questions about the corpus's values, rules, and structure by querying the Neo4j graph via MCP instead of grepping source files. Use for "what does X do", "which members of a catalog...", "what kind of thing is...", consistency lookups, and metamodel questions.
---

# Querying the rules graph

Boundary context: `python -m graph docs ontology-doctrine`

## Rendering a gate

The pending changeset's facts live in the delta report records
(graph/reports/delta-report.json): each verdict carries a code, a
subject, particulars, a remedy, and a plain-English reference number
(`ref`). The
technical rendering (graph/reports/delta.md) is the forensics layer —
link it on request, never lead with it.

Procedure:

1. **Header**: artifact name — world — "enters canon on your
   approval" — pending count. One approval addresses one world's
   canon: when an artifact touches several worlds, run one intake
   per world and present their gates together under one header,
   grouped by world (T4) — each world's sign-off commits only to
   that world. A single world is named once.
2. **Every verdict and ceremony record becomes a pending item** in
   the four-move anatomy (T6): the question in the designer's terms;
   current state and proposed state with evidence inline in the
   artifact's native form; implications; the ask restated as a direct
   action. To name a subject in the designer's terms, query canon:
   the subject ref gives its identity; its kind and its own doc text
   give what to call it and how to describe it. Never render a
   record's `message` field to the designer — that is the machinery's
   sentence; compose the item from `code`, `subject`, `data`, and
   canon. (A few records still carry their facts only in `message` —
   producers that predate the record shape. For those, take the facts
   *from* the message but re-voice them under the tenets; never quote
   the machinery's sentence. Each such record is conversion debt on
   the machinery's side, not license to parse prose elsewhere.)
3. **Frame by severity** (T8, provisional): a gap the designer can
   fill on the spot is a request; a structural stop is a plain
   verdict plus what would clear it.
4. **Reference numbers** (T10): every item ends with
   `⟨subject · ref⟩` using the record's `ref` key.
5. **Compress the clean** (T7): everything that checked clean is one
   line with counts, expandable on request.
6. **Capture rulings as records** (T15): each resolution — and the
   designer's stated reason, verbatim — is authored into the round as
   the Judgment machinery's question/decision citizens, entering
   canon through the same approval as the work itself.

## Round scope (owner-ruled)

**The submitter chooses the round's scope at the start of every
sitting** — one chapter, a subsystem batch, a paragraph; the machinery
imposes no cadence. Open a campaign session by asking what this
round's scope is (default: a subsystem batch). Inside a
batch, the per-chapter loop runs agent-side; the submitter sits one
plan gate and one collated diff gate. The owner is trialing the
breakdowns firsthand in clean sessions; when multi-submitter arrives,
cadence becomes a per-person graph-resident preference.

## Taking in an artifact

- Work the whole artifact; batch judgment calls to the gate (T13).
  Interrupt only for a true blocker — a call that would distort how
  everything after it is read.
- Group inferences by pattern for one confirmation each (T12), every
  family naming its instances.
- The artifact's medium sets the evidence form (T3): quote the
  sentence, show the region, timestamp the passage, link the page.

## The Completeness ruling comes first

**Read the menu from the graph, not from memory** (levels are doc-bearing
Ordered citizens):

```cypher
MATCH (level:Archetype)-[:INSTANCE_OF]->(:Archetype {name: 'Completeness'})
RETURN level.rank, level.name, level.doc ORDER BY level.rank
```

Then apply the two-axis test **with the owner, before extracting
anything**:

1. Does an agent need the inner workings? (An in-world character
   reasoning "how does this work for me?" — yes. Selecting a tool
   from a catalog — no.)
2. Do we own the source? (Our corpus — yes. A third-party tool's
   docs — no.)

Both yes → **transcribed** (full YAML program; signature derived).
Inner workings no, or source not ours → **attested** (asserted signature +
prose link + `approved_hash`) or **cited** (name + link).
The failure mode is defaulting to maximum completeness because you can.
Don't.

## The convergence loop

When a draft must reach parity with a source (chapter regeneration, the
book campaign), run the loop — never hand-polish toward a quiet judge:

1. **Cold draft, fenced**: every draft sentence traces to a graph
   record you can name. Canon gaps stay red on purpose — smuggling
   source text into the draft hides real thinness. State the fence's
   honesty limits aloud (prior exposure is discipline, not amnesia; the
   judge is the objective check).
2. **Judge, then burn down only what needs no one's judgment**
   (findings are ROWS in the reading room — query the open set
   beside its sections, update statuses as you resolve; the prose
   report is a rendering, not the record): a
   finding is agent-resolvable ONLY when its fix is fully determined by
   the graph and rulings already on record — presentation-form
   mismatches, rewording a draft sentence toward the source where the
   graph already holds the fact, deleting the draft's own inventions.
   Any fix that would add, drop, or bend meaning is not yours; it goes
   to the gate. When in doubt, escalate. The goal is that the human
   never sees finding 3 of 64 — and never misses one that was theirs
   to rule.
3. **One collated escalation gate**: everything needing a human word,
   grouped by resolution channel — canon gaps (become intake), flavor
   (verbatim-carried or Approved Omission), examples (per the
   standing examples Decision on the graph), harness defects (their
   own issues, with a one-line
   engine ask). Each group states what each answer does.
4. **Rulings recorded by identity** (Decision rows, Approved Omission
   rows), then regenerate and re-judge. Converged parity = zero
   UNAPPROVED differences — the report may stay non-empty forever, so
   long as every line carries a ruling.

Standing rules the loop rides on:

- **Every PASS names its judged surface.** A green scorecard once
  lied because prose inside procedure-cited sections was unjudged.
  Unjudged space is either zero or declared aloud in the same breath
  as the verdict.
- **Verify presentation artifacts in the audience's renderer.** A
  diagram verified in VS Code shipped unreadable on GitHub three times.
  The acceptance test is the renderer the audience actually uses.
- **Question triage at phase boundaries**: every retro/phase-cut
  sitting opens with the carried Questions — rule some, park the rest,
  never let the list grow silently.

name: The default path (short; machinery engages only on signals)

properties.body:
## The default path (short; machinery engages only on signals)

1. **Understand as a habit** — the Method runs internally (ask,
   audience, artifacts, person, organization, composition — including
   the standing UNIT question: which axes — structural / temporal /
   spatial — what hierarchy; "none" and "sequence-of" are legal;
   "cannot tell" escalates). Surface to the owner ONLY what is
   genuinely ambiguous, batched into one question sheet, conversation
   available on any line of it.
2. **Work** — one agent per unit of work, with a brief that is a
   constraint-set + provisioned data + model tier (never a persona);
   iterate against the deterministic judge where one exists.
3. **Floor + present** — the honest floor: remaining disagreements
   named and classified (gap / taste / error). Present the COMPLETED
   artifact with the floor census and margin attached — never
   fragments, never diffs.
4. **Iterate / consent** — harvest owner comments (deduce
   defect/taste/question; never demand a format; convert theirs if
   they use one); answer questions first; taste persists as steering.
   Consent is asked when canon mutates or work publishes — not as a
   completion ritual.

Engagement signals that bring machinery in: no deterministic judge →
critique ensemble (weight inversely proportional to judge strength);
mute single-shot generator → composition ensemble ahead of the shot;
units > 1 → shard by unit + a cross-unit coherence expert; repeated
worker/judge disagreement → second opinion; stuck → escalate with work
shown. When a gate engages, review BRIEF CONTENT, not cast topology.
Plan generation is one seeded casting step, never a meta-ensemble.

## The flow

### 1. Recon (read-only; no human) — sealed reading FIRST
**The reading is sealed before the mapping opens** (owner-ruled): read
and comprehend the artifact ON ITS OWN TERMS — structure, vocabulary,
fact-grain claims, its own internal contradictions — BEFORE any canon
query. A reader whose head is full of canon assimilates the artifact
to existing categories before it has finished speaking, harmonizes
contradictions it should surface, and misses genuine deviations; the
kernel (metaontology structure) may inform the reading, project canon
may not. Only when comprehension is complete does the mapping open:
each artifact-local claim judged against canon — same-as / extends /
new / contradicts — every mapping a recorded Opinion with confidence,
low confidence batching to the owner's question sheet. (Held as
discipline — the lens system that will enforce it physically is
designed and built (the engine's lens module and its lenses design record (design/ in the engine repo; graph/engine_docs/design/ inside an installed engine package)); the seal
becomes physical when the declarations take graph residence at the
owner's gate.)

Open the reading room first: `python -m graph comprehend <artifact>`
fingerprints the source and builds its structure (section tree, bodies,
order, embedded-table refs) in the comprehension workspace, filing the
flat archive under `graph/comprehension/`. Canon is the subject matter,
never the document — the artifact's insides live here, not as canon
citizens; artifact quirks
(duplicate headings, odd nesting) are absorbed silently, never surfaced
to the submitter. Then read the source cold. Identify — by **semantic
comprehension, never word search** — every entity, relationship, and
rule it asserts, whatever the casing discipline. Resolve pronouns and indirect references; ambiguity
that survives multiple passes becomes an owner question, never a guess.
Resolve every candidate through the graph (read-only Cypher + the term
index; `python -m graph terms` is the mechanical backstop, not the
method). Check the stub worklist (`MATCH (s:Archetype {stub: true})`) and
prior Judgment rows — the term may already be a known-open item. Bucket
findings: *relates-to* / *introduces* / *uncertain*, with grades.
**A machinery risk you can verify during recon is a recon task, not a
risk to carry into the round**: read the code or run the tool now, and
if the gap is real, its ask joins the owner's collated sheet as a
numbered question. A "named risk" in the plan that a five-minute read
would have settled resurfaces later as a mid-round interjection — the
costlier shape.

### 2. The plan gate (the approver)
Present the what's-this-about proposal, **leading with the implications
preview**: what the approver GETS, what they LOSE or change, what it
AFFORDS later — each with a concrete example from the corpus. Then the
interview, per ontology-intake's discipline (three tiers; scenario
questions; the owner names everything and rules everything —
explicitly, never by silence). The interview arrives as ONE collated
question sheet — every question batched with its cited evidence,
named tension, consequences, and a recommendation; serial pinging is
not a permitted shape (see that skill's interview step).
Procedure-shaped content inside the source
follows procedure-intake at this point. Nothing has been written
anywhere.

### 3. Schema is ground on the graph — and changes by ceremony
The schema stratum (the concept citizens and their edges) is ground
truth on the graph itself: post-bootstrap machinery reads it from the
graph, never from a schema file, and the schema anchor's version
auto-stamps from the event-log sequence at apply. **Schema changes
ride the schema ceremony**: an owner-gated round may add a new
DECLARED concept (the Archetype arrives WITH its DECLARED_IN edge, and
usually INSTANCE_OF into its parent), birth a new LABEL (a
spec-carrying row arriving WITH its DECLARED_IN edge, permitted only
when the base holds no ground rows under it — nothing yet underneath,
so nothing moves), edit a schema row's doc text,
add an ALIAS to a label's spec (a new surface spelling reading as an
existing citizen — additions only, each target existing in the base or
born by the same round), or
remove an UNREFERENCED schema row — the delta report itemizes these
under its marked ceremony section, and the owner's approval of that
round IS the ceremony ruling. Everything else on the stratum — changes
to existing labels, other spec/catalog changes, renames, referenced
removals — still
refuses by name (data moves underneath those; they ride the migration
charter) and PARKS as a Question at the plan gate for the owner to
rule and sequence; it never blocks the fact-plane work that doesn't
need it, and it is never worked around with a lesser encoding. Facts
whose schema doesn't exist yet wait with their Question.

One mirror rides ceremony edits that change what the bootstrap file
declares: when the corpus keeps a from-sources bootstrap file guarded
by a round-trip parity suite, that file gains the same change in the
same change set — a doc edit on a CONCEPT row (a schema row without an
embedded spec) mirrors its doc text into the concept entry, and an
ADDED ALIAS mirrors into the label entry's aliases map. The suite
compares the loader's specs against the graph's and fails on the
divergence. A doc edit on a LABEL row alone needs no mirror; that doc
lives on the row.

### 4. Scratch authoring (agent + machine)
Reset scratch first (`python -m graph restore --database scratch`, using
the KB's own working-copy name if its settings declare one) — stale
scratch produces phantom diffs, and the round machinery refuses a copy
whose in-band identity does not match the round. **The standing first authoring move is
clearing the previous round's debts**: stamp that round's shipped PR
link onto its Judgment rows, and land any edges it deferred under
marker rows whose endpoints now exist in canon. A round that skips the
opening move leaves the debt to compound — one round of lag is the
design; two is a backlog. Then author **ground facts** through the
`neo4j-scratch` MCP connection, the way agents naturally work: create,
query your own work, fix, iterate.
- MATCH existing endpoints, MERGE only the new node/relationship (a
  whole-path MERGE duplicates existing nodes and trips the uniqueness
  constraint).
- Every non-obvious fact carries its receipt as properties: `from_text`
  (verbatim source quote), `source` (where), `grade: 'agent-proposed'`.
  Receipts are review evidence — canonize deliberately never renders
  them into files.
- NEVER write derived edge types (INSTANCE_OF, projections, MENTIONS,
  lift edges, KNOWN_AT…) or machine labels (Archetype/Step/Outcome) —
  the delta lint rejects them with the reason.
- **Identity stays single-label; membership is multi.** Each citizen is
  keyed and exported by exactly one roster label — its home, its
  catalog, its source — and that never changes. But a citizen may be
  declared a member of more than one concept: author a ground
  `DECLARED_MEMBER_OF` edge FROM the citizen TO a Concept Archetype,
  carrying a required `basis` rationale, and derivation folds it into
  the citizen's `INSTANCE_OF`. So a gem its roster makes a Treasure can
  ALSO be declared a Tool while a sibling gem on the same roster is not
  — an overlap no longer needs the shared-catalog-vocabulary workaround.
  The edge only ADDS membership and never re-homes the citizen: its
  target must be a subject-matter Concept (never a Facet, never another
  label's Archetype), and `INSTANCE_OF` itself stays never-authored —
  the fold computes it.
- A concept Archetype born by THIS round's schema edit does not exist
  in scratch (scratch is cut pre-schema from the backup) — anchor
  Judgment ABOUT edges for brand-new labels to value citizens instead.
  The same constraint blocks DOMAIN ground edges: an edge whose target
  citizen is born by this round's schema edit cannot be authored in
  scratch at all. Declare exactly those edges in the round's STITCH
  file — `graph/proposals/current/stitch.json`, a JSON list of
  connections in the proposal document's edge shape (type, from_label,
  from_name, to_label, to_name, optional props). They ride the same
  approval and land in the same apply, after re-derivation births
  their endpoints; the delta report itemizes them under "Stitch" and
  refuses any that don't genuinely need it. Never re-point a deferred
  edge at a lesser endpoint that happens to exist. (Marker-row
  deferrals from earlier rounds still land at the opening move; new
  rounds use the stitch.)
- Provenance URLs on Judgment rows: take the repo from `gh repo view`,
  never guess the owner (a guessed owner once landed in a whole batch
  of rows and forced a correction round).

### 5. Delta + self-review (agent + machine)
`python -m graph delta` — the itemized, linted changeset
(graph/reports/delta.md). Read it against your own plan: every
surprise is either fixed in scratch or demoted to the uncertain bucket.
Lint violations are yours to fix before the approver ever sees the
report. Then `python -m graph canonize` (dry run) — confirm everything
renders deterministically; a REVIEW-REQUIRED item at this stage means a
schema ruling was missed: go back to step 3 (or the plan gate if it is a
genuinely new decision).

### 6. The diff gate (the approver)
Present the delta report — and offer the Bloom walk on scratch (the
proposal is explorable as a graph before it exists in canon). The
approver resolves the uncertain bucket: rule, "give it a go" (back to
step 4), or park as Judgment citizens. Approval here is approval of the
exact changeset.

**Mid-round refactor pressure is never round scope.** A tempting
rename, a structural cleanup the round doesn't need — park it as a
Judgment row routed via HAS_DISCIPLINE / HAS_AUDIENCE to the project's
Discipline and Audience citizens. The kernel declares those two
classes only; each project's values are its own, disclosed by the team
or discerned from real cases — the first round that needs a value
proposes it at the escalation gate like any new vocabulary. Parked
pressure is design input for a later phase, never scope creep.

### 7. Approve, canonize + drain to zero (machine)
When the approver rules "approved" at the diff gate, record it:
`python -m graph approve` (the record names the human; the proposal's
content hash is frozen — apply replays exactly what was reviewed, and
refuses by name if scratch or the base moved after approval). Then
`python -m graph canonize --apply` — GRAPH-NATIVE since the flip:
no file is edited. Apply verifies the live database still
matches the backup, applies the pinned changeset to the ground layer,
re-derives every machine layer, loads canon, re-exports the backup FROM
the database, and writes the EVENT LOG (chained entry in
`graph/proposals/applied.log` + the delta's inverse) — all one command,
refusing collated and writing nothing on any failure. Then the ritual:
pytest → commit the export + round archive + applied.log line in one
change set. The next round cuts scratch fresh
(`python -m graph restore --database scratch`). `load` and
`export --from-sources` are bootstrap scaffolding only.

### 8. Bookkeeping (same standards as any round)
Judgment rows for parked items (they can flow through scratch + canonize
too), the ontology TODO block, the glossary stage (classify every
unresolved-term hit; shrink the stub worklist), skills updated with any
lesson learned in-session — **stated timelessly and domain-neutrally**:
no issue numbers, no dates, no project vocabulary; the rule stands on
its own, with an agnostic example where one earns its keep. PR
provenance lands via the NEXT round's standing opening move (step 4) —
the shipped PR's link cannot exist before ship, so the stamp is always
one round behind by design. Definition
of Done applies: tests, docs, skills ride along.

# The front door

The door is a separate concept from the jobs it invokes. It owns the
only conversation the designer sees; the jobs own the work. Its
constitution is the fifteen tenets in the engine's front-door-tenets
design record (design/ in the engine repo; graph/engine_docs/design/
inside an installed package) — read them before speaking. This skill
is the operating procedure that puts them into practice.

**The invariant:** the door never parses prose for facts and never
speaks machinery words. Facts come from two places only — the typed
records the jobs emit, and canon itself, queried live. If a fact is
not in a record and not in canon, the door does not know it, and says
so (T14).

## The invariants (medium-independent)

1. **Facts come from provenance, only.** Every asserting element — a
   number, a name, a relationship, a depicted attribute — must trace to
   a citizen, or on a cold graph to the source artifact itself. If
   neither holds anything, that is a GAP surfaced to the owner as a
   question, never filled by invention.
2. **Steering shapes presentation, never facts.** Steering that would
   contradict canon gets surfaced, not silently obeyed.
3. **Nothing semantically omitted or distorted** within the request's
   scope; presentation free inside that boundary.
4. **The raw ask + context ride verbatim** into every brief. Derived
   context supplements, never replaces.

# The maintenance loop

Boundary context: `python -m graph docs ontology-doctrine`

The graph is canon (the flip); `graph/export/` is its committed backup,
written FROM the database. Source files (CSVs, overlays) are bootstrap
scaffolding and may legitimately lag canon. The verbs, by situation:

1. `python -m graph restore` — rebuild the live database from the
   committed backup alone (no sources involved). DRILL PASSED means the
   database re-serializes byte-identical to the backup. This is the
   reset for a stale or drifted live database, and the routine
   reconcile step after a merge.
2. `python -m graph restore --database scratch` — cut a fresh round:
   scratch becomes a clone of canon with the base pinned. Run it before
   any scratch authoring and after any schema edit.
3. `make validate` — parse sources and schema against the ontology,
   writing `graph/reports/validation.md`. **Errors** block (broken
   ontology or file); **warnings/info** are data findings and never
   block.
4. `python -m graph rederive` — after a schema-bootstrap edit
   (`graph/ontology.yaml`): re-derives the machine layers over the
   unchanged ground facts and re-exports the backup. It refuses,
   collated, if the schema has errors or if ground facts would change —
   ground changes go through the delta path, never through derivation.
5. **Backup coherence is enforced**: any change that alters the graph
   must re-export the backup in the same change set — the golden test
   (`tests/test_golden.py`) proves the backup's derived layers agree
   with what `derive()` recomputes. A golden failure after an
   intentional change isn't an error; it's the reminder.
6. `make check` — canned consistency checks
   (`graph/cypher/checks/*.cypher`) against the live DB. Two species:
   checks headed `// expect: empty` are ASSERTIONS — rows mean an
   integrity bug and the command exits non-zero. The rest are FINDING
   REPORTS — rows are open data questions (candidate Judgments),
   informational by design. A failed assertion blocks; findings never
   do.
7. Spot-verify via MCP (counts per label, a known query from the
   cookbook).

`make test` runs the full pytest suite. Bootstrap-era verbs (`load`,
`export --from-sources`) survive only as scaffolding for building a
graph from sources before canon exists — never part of a normal round.

## The trace and the margin

- Every run records who was cast, what they were told, what they
  cited, what the judge ruled, what escalated. Claims about runs cite
  the trace; recollection is not a source.
- The trace machinery is the engine's runs module (graph.runs): open with new_run(brief,
  started), record judgments with add_row (question / answer /
  decision / opinion — decided_by names the agent, confidence graded
  honestly), and file the archive with write_archive under graph/runs/
  at run end. Ratifying a row into canon goes through the ordinary
  approval ceremony; promotion(run, name) packages the citation.
- Agent judgments made mid-run (mapping choices, low-confidence calls)
  are Opinions with confidence, kept on the run's record and surfaced
  as MARGIN ANNOTATIONS inline in the presented artifact where
  confidence is low or canon was silent. The owner replies in the same
  margin; an owner catch on an UNFLAGGED decision means confidence was
  miscalibrated — record it.
- Annotations anchor to (artifact, span) from day one. The machinery
  is the engine's runs module: pass anchor={artifact, start, end, text} to
  add_row (the exact quote is mandatory — it re-locates the span if
  the artifact moves); margin(run, fingerprint, artifact_text) reads
  the floor census in span order; render_margin presents artifact and
  annotations together; write_archive(run, dir, artifacts) refuses
  any anchor whose quote is not really in its artifact.
- Before saying "done" after any fix round, re-check everything the
  owner previously approved — a fix must not silently break prior
  approvals; a defect class the owner caught once is checked by
  machine thereafter. The machinery is `python -m graph corpus`
  (the engine's corpus module; the KB keeps its ledger at graph/corpus/floors.jsonl): run it
  before any "done" report, and when the owner blesses a new
  expectation or catches an unflagged decision, record the floor
  (record_floor: guard test node id, scope, plain-words expectation,
  provenance) in the same change set as the fix.

## What the door never does

- Never invents domain vocabulary, opinions, or design decisions —
  the designer rules; the door informs (T9).
- Never shows machinery words on any surface (T2): no database,
  graph, delta, scratch, round, lint. The system's acts have one
  vocabulary: *enters canon*, *pending your approval*.
- Never presents an item that cannot be ruled on from itself alone
  (T6).
- Never answers without a citation (T11), and never fabricates one:
  an uncitable answer is an absence, said plainly.

## When answering

Lead with the answer, cite counts precisely (say when placeholders are
included/excluded), and if a query surfaces something inconsistent, report it
as a finding — don't fix data unasked.
## Boundary rules

---

The tenets are domain-agnostic and travel with the engine, like the
intake conduct before them. The machinery's own reports — the typed
records and the technical rendering — are unchanged underneath; the
door is a reader of records and canon, never a second source of
truth.

The tenets are the same everywhere; the door is not. Each world's
door is expected to be **tailored to that world's experience**: the
conduct trunk ships with the engine at whatever version the world
pins, the voice is learned live from that world's canon (T1), and a
world keeps its own local skills beside the engine's. Two worlds at
different pins run different conduct on purpose — skew is a chosen
consequence of pinning ([engine-as-corpus.md](engine-as-corpus.md)).
## Conduct

# Front Door Tenets

The front door is the voice that stands between the designer and the
machinery. It is a separate concept from the jobs it invokes — query,
ingest, generation — and it owns the only conversation the designer
sees: approval gates, questions and answers, ingestion, annotations,
debate. The jobs keep their technical surfaces for agents and
forensics; the door renders everything designer-facing under the
tenets below, settled by owner interview, 2026-08-24 through
2026-08-26.

The reference rendering (a text ingestion in an imaginary world —
the artifact could as well be an image, a model, a song, or a link):

```
COMBAT MANEUVERS — Emberfall · enters canon on your approval · 2 items pending

1. Is Grit also a Combat Skill?

   Your new text treats it that way ("Grit functions as a
   combat skill during rally checks", ¶4); today canon
   knows it only as a Trait. It can be both — canon just
   keeps the why on record, in your words.

   → Tell me why Grit is also a Combat Skill, or tell me
     that sentence shouldn't be read that way.
   ⟨grit · missing-reason⟩

2. Does Rally's definition change?

   Your new text reads: "Rally is the moment, after nerve
   is retested, a routed unit turns to fight." (¶9). Canon's
   current wording: "the moment a routed unit turns to
   fight." Approving makes the after-retest reading explicit
   everywhere Rally is used.

   → Approve the new wording, or keep the current.
   ⟨rally · description-edit⟩

Checked clean: 14 additions, no conflicts.        (ask to see all)
```
